content:
We need to move from a "references.md" document to a more specific "provenance.md" document, that will track every element of a pack change: it will explain why it came to be, what was the source, what was the reason, who was the actor (or possibly what was their organizational role), what was the LLM model that made the decision, why was it decided to be made into a rule, or skill, or task, or check, or declared check, why were other plausible options rejected, why was prose transformed to check, why a predicable skill trigger was added, why was a task automerge rule added. All of these could be considered comments or extra context for the rule/test, but they are not - they are noise that hinders the simple usage and execution of the pack elements. They are, however, crucial to pack maintenance and updates, wither in terms of tracking reasons, the possiblilty to update based on false premises, or conflicts of instrcutions, and their origins. So basically - every element of a pack should be tracked thusly. When I say "element of a pack" I mean that there's a guideline that the pack maintains, with by prose to tell agents what to do, by checks that will verify predictably, by skill prose, and skill loading rules. I suspect we should have a folder of provenance files, one for each element. The provenance folder should not be vendored to the using repos (I think references.md isn't as well). We should do our best to backfill provenance files for existing packs by tracking git history of a pack. The provenance shouldn't track minor edits to rules (like a code comment chagne, but a minor edit to prose could be important and should be tracked, if for example, a rule changed the language for "you must check that..." to "you should check" because of a human decision or a prose-writing guideline change). We should see about correctly marking all elements of a pack, assigining them provenance files, and then start filling. It is ok to have one "element" with one provenance tracker, that covers a prose rule, a skill and a check. We should strive for more independance, but sometimes that's not possible. Provenanace should (must) be tracked on repo local packs, and canon-curation/promote should grab that history with the promoted elements. Provenance files should not be checked for barriers, because they refer to everything almost by definition. They should also be seldom edited, and often appended. Provenanace is a log of decisions, not the description of the current state. Let's reiterate that - it is not, and should not be attempted to be a description of the current rules, just why they are this way. Hopefully this change in how we maintain packs should be limited to the workings of the claudinite-growth pack (excpet for the actual provenanace update). If there are update to other rules - explain them. We should change these mechanisms as a separate change from the massive provenance update. Take into account different trypes of packs: repo-local, org-local, user-preferences (assume it's a pack), claudinite canon, tech-vendor authored packs, process/rules-of-thumb packs (like testing), or others, if you can think of any.

 I think it would be best for your process to not only design a plan, but also to consider how the end result would look like for a specific pack, including the provenanace files, the data stored in them, and linking them to the elements. I htink packs/chrome-extension is a good candidate. It would also be good for me to see the "end result" of your suggestion.

Analyze everything I said, create a design for this. Try to find edge cases, data explosions, missing elements, privacy issues. If you can think of other benefits we'll get from this mechanism - please list them too. This is not a technically hard problem, but it deals with knowledge management for all packs, and all future repos using claudinite, so we need to make the best plan going forward here.

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

We need to move from a "references.md" document to a more specific "provenance.md" document, that will track every element of a pack change: it will explain why it came to be, what was the source, what was the reason, who was the actor (or possibly what was their organizational role), what was the LLM model that made the decision, why was it decided to be made into a rule, or skill, or task, or check, or declared check, why were other plausible options rejected, why was prose transformed to check, why a predicable skill trigger was added, why was a task automerge rule added. All of these could be considered comments or extra context for the rule/test, but they are not - they are noise that hinders the simple usage and execution of the pack elements. They are, however, crucial to pack maintenance and updates, wither in terms of tracking reasons, the possiblilty to update based on false premises, or conflicts of instrcutions, and their origins. So basically - every element of a pack should be tracked thusly. When I say "element of a pack" I mean that there's a guideline that the pack maintains, with by prose to tell agents what to do, by checks that will verify predictably, by skill prose, and skill loading rules. I suspect we should have a folder of provenance files, one for each element. The provenance folder should not be vendored to the using repos (I think references.md isn't as well). We should do our best to backfill provenance files for existing packs by tracking git history of a pack. The provenance shouldn't track minor edits to rules (like a code comment chagne, but a minor edit to prose could be important and should be tracked, if for example, a rule changed the language for "you must check that..." to "you should check" because of a human decision or a prose-writing guideline change). We should see about correctly marking all elements of a pack, assigining them provenance files, and then start filling. It is ok to have one "element" with one provenance tracker, that covers a prose rule, a skill and a check. We should strive for more independance, but sometimes that's not possible. Provenanace should (must) be tracked on repo local packs, and canon-curation/promote should grab that history with the promoted elements. Provenance files should not be checked for barriers, because they refer to everything almost by definition. They should also be seldom edited, and often appended. Provenanace is a log of decisions, not the description of the current state. Let's reiterate that - it is not, and should not be attempted to be a description of the current rules, just why they are this way. Hopefully this change in how we maintain packs should be limited to the workings of the claudinite-growth pack (excpet for the actual provenanace update). If there are update to other rules - explain them. We should change these mechanisms as a separate change from the massive provenance update. Take into account different trypes of packs: repo-local, org-local, user-preferences (assume it's a pack), claudinite canon, tech-vendor authored packs, process/rules-of-thumb packs (like testing), or others, if you can think of any.

 I think it would be best for your process to not only design a plan, but also to consider how the end result would look like for a specific pack, including the provenanace files, the data stored in them, and linking them to the elements. I htink packs/chrome-extension is a good candidate. It would also be good for me to see the "end result" of your suggestion.

Analyze everything I said, create a design for this. Try to find edge cases, data explosions, missing elements, privacy issues. If you can think of other benefits we'll get from this mechanism - please list them too. This is not a technically hard problem, but it deals with knowledge management for all packs, and all future repos using claudinite, so we need to make the best plan going forward here.

I htink packs/chrome-extension is a good candidate. It would also be good for me to see the "end result" of your suggestion.

Analyze everything I said, create a design for this. Try to find edge cases, data explosions, missing elements, privacy issues. If you can think of other benefits we'll get from this mechanism - please list them too. This is not a technically hard problem, but it deals with knowledge management for all packs, and all future repos using claudinite, so we need to make the best plan going forward here.
