1	# Provenance — the decision log behind every pack element
2	
3	> **Status: not implemented.** A design under discussion; nothing below describes how the
4	> repository works today.
5	
6	A pack carries guidelines, and each guideline reaches a session through one or more **carriers**:
7	a rule in `RULES.md`, a skill with its load triggers, a coded or declared check, a task with its
8	policy. The carriers say *what* to do, and they are rationed to that. Nothing in them says why
9	they read as they do, who decided, from what evidence, why this carrier and this trigger and not
10	another, or what would have to become true for the guideline to go. That record is
11	**provenance**: one append-only file per element, in a `provenance/` folder beside the carriers,
12	read by maintenance and never by a working session.
13	
14	| Surface | Question it answers | Who reads it |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| the carriers — `RULES.md`, `skills/`, the checks, `tasks/`, `pack.mjs` | what does a session do | every session in every repo that declares the pack |
17	| `provenance/<element>.md` | why the element is as it is — its mechanism above all — and what would retire it | the growth and curation passes, a promote run, a maintainer |
18	| `README.md` | how a repository uses the pack and its elements | a person adopting the pack, or reaching for one of its elements |
19	
20	Provenance is a log of decisions. It is never a description of the current rule: an entry that
21	restates what the carrier says is wrong by construction, and a reader who wants the rule reads the
22	carrier.
23	
24	## 1. The element, its id, and its file
25	
26	An **element** is one guideline the pack maintains. It has exactly one provenance file, and the
27	file's name is the element's **id**: a slug chosen when the element is born, for the guideline
28	rather than its current wording, and never renamed afterwards (a rename breaks every entry and
29	every override that cites it). The id is also how each carrier references the file:
30	
31	| Carrier | Its reference to the element |
32	|---|---|
33	| a coded or declared check | its check id; a slash becomes a hyphen (`cer/version-bumped` → `cer-version-bumped.md`) |
34	| a skill — the body, the description, every `force-load-on-*` trigger | its directory name |
35	| a task — the declaration, its preconditions, `expected_outcome`, `automerge`, the worker | its task id |
36	| the manifest — fingerprint, `requires`, routing guidance, seeding, the pack's own existence and name | `pack` |
37	| a prose rule — a top-level bullet of `RULES.md`, or of a `SKILL.md` where the bullet has a history of its own | a **marker** ending the rule: `… never a filesystem walk. (url-filter-host-operators)` |
38	
39	A check, a skill and a task already carry a stable id, so their files are named by it and nothing
40	is added to them. A prose rule has none, and the marker gives it one: the reference from the prose
41	to its file, and the stable id by which a member's override or `accept` entry can name the rule
42	and survive its rewording — the one obligation the layering design places on the corpus, paid
43	once. The marker is the only thing this design adds to injected prose, and it is rationed like the
44	prose: a slug of two to four words, so a rewording never has to touch it. It costs a few tokens
45	per rule, two to three times what a numeric marker costs — on the order of a thousand tokens
46	across a member that loads two hundred rules, out of a budget of fifteen thousand — and nothing
47	cheaper carries both the reference and the id.
48	
49	One file normally covers one carrier. It covers several when they are one guideline — a prose rule
50	and the check that enforces its checkable half, a rule and the skill it delegates to — and then
51	the file is named by the check or the skill, and the rule's marker cites that name. Independence
52	where it is real, one file where it is not; a carrier names exactly one live file, and a check or
53	a skill is never split across files.
54	
55	A skill is one element, named by its directory, and its file is where the skill's **mechanism** is
56	accounted for: why a skill rather than prose, why these `force-load-on-*` triggers and these
57	paths rather than others, why the description names the moments it names. A bullet inside a skill
58	earns an element of its own — its own marker and file — only where it has a decision history of
59	its own; every other bullet is the skill's, and the skill's file records their decisions as titled
60	entries. That is what keeps a long procedure from minting thirty files while letting the one
61	bullet that was fought over keep its own log.
62	
63	### What is not an element, and where its decision lives
64	
65	Everything else a pack directory holds is either a property of an element, whose decisions go on
66	that element's file, or an artifact whose decision is the pack's, or evidence:
67	
68	| Artifact | Its decision is recorded on |
69	|---|---|
70	| a check's `severity`, `scope`, `relevantWhen` gate, `since` date, `failureMessage` and `fix` text | the check's file (`born`, `severity-changed`, `reworded`) |
71	| a skill's `description` and every `force-load-on-*` trigger | the skill's file (`trigger-changed`) |
72	| a task's preconditions, `expected_outcome`, `automerge`, `agent_model`, worker | the task's file (`policy-changed`) |
73	| the manifest: `detect`/`marker`, `requires`, `ruleRoutingGuidance`, `seededByDefault`, `hidden`, `env`, adoption `questions`, `adoptionHandover`, `contributes` and `contributedRules`, `merge-rules.json`, the badge | `pack` |
74	| the pack's own existence, name, split or collapse; a rename-map entry for an absorbed pack | `pack` of the pack that exists afterwards |
75	| stubs and migrations | their own module headers, plus a `pack` entry for the decision to ship them |
76	| tests and fixtures | nothing — a fixture is evidence, cited from the check's entry |
77	| `README.md` | nothing — it says how the pack is used (below), and every sentence of history in it moves onto the entry it is evidence for (§6) |
78	| `VERSIONS.md`, `directory.GENERATED.md`, the rule inventory | nothing — derived, never decided |
79	| a member's `accept` waiver, severity override or `disabledTasks` entry | the member's settings file, whose `reason` is the record; no provenance file |
80	| a design doc, a capture on the conversation-logs branch, a tracker comment, a pull request body | evidence — cited by an entry, never copied into one |
81	
82	### The README beside them
83	
84	A pack's `README.md` is for the person adopting the pack or reaching for one of its elements, and
85	it carries only what that person does with it: when the pack activates, what each check demands
86	and what satisfies it, when a skill is the thing to load, what the task does to the repository,
87	and the catalog of what the pack carries. It never carries how an element came to be, what it
88	replaced, why its id reads as it does, what an earlier shape did, or how the pack is maintained.
89	The test is the sentence: a date, a pull request number, an "until", a "was", a "kept as it was"
90	or a "distilled from" is a decision, and a decision is an entry on the element's file — `pack`
91	for the pack's own shape, the element's own file for the rest. The maintainer's procedure is not
92	the README's either: it is the growth skills', forced when a pack file is edited (§3), and the
93	provenance those skills append to. What is left is shorter, and it is read by the one reader a
94	README has.
95	
96	### The file
97	
98	A file is its entries and nothing else — no header, no front matter, no restatement of what it
99	covers, because what it covers is derived: the carriers that name it, by id or by marker, and
100	`check` prints them. An empty file is an element whose history has not been written yet.
101	
102	```
103	## 2026-07-18 · born · promoted from a member's local pack (#319)
104	- **Source:** the member's own site rule, gated on `PageStateMatcher.pageUrl`, matched a
105	  lookalike host.
106	- **Reason:** `hostSuffix` is a raw string suffix, so `example.com` also matches
107	  `evilexample.com`; nothing in the API says so at the call site.
108	- **Actor:** the growth-promote run, merged by @missingbulb (owner).
109	- **Mechanism:** prose. A check would have to know which behaviours are origin-sensitive; the
110	  signature (a bare `hostSuffix`) is not the violation.
111	- **Retire when:** Chrome documents `hostSuffix` as label-bounded, or `UrlFilter` is removed.
112	- **Landed:** #319 · pack version 1.
113	
114	## 2026-07-27 · reworded · the corpus-wide "when + what + one non-obvious fact" pass (#467)
115	- **Reason:** the `hostContains` clause and the lookalike sentence restated the rule; both cut.
116	- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
117	- **Landed:** #467 · pack version 1.
118	```
119	
120	An **entry** opens `## <YYYY-MM-DD> · <kind> · <one line>` and carries bold-labelled fields, one
121	per bullet, continuation lines indented. Entries are appended in date order and never edited. An
122	element whose last entry is `retired` is retired; nothing else says so.
123	
124	The **kinds** are closed: `born`, `reworded`, `strengthened`, `weakened`, `split`, `merged`,
125	`moved` (a carrier change — rule to skill, pack to pack), `converted` (prose to check),
126	`trigger-changed` (a skill's load trigger or description), `policy-changed` (a task's `automerge`,
127	`expected_outcome` or preconditions), `severity-changed`, `reaffirmed`, `promoted`, `retired`.
128	`strengthened` and `weakened` are the modality grade — "must" to "should" is a decision, and the
129	kind says which way it went.
130	
131	The **fields**, each written only when there is something to say — a field with nothing behind it
132	is omitted, never filled with a placeholder, because a reader must be able to tell what the record
133	knows from what it does not:
134	
135	- `Source` — where the lesson came from: an incident, a document, a request, a capture (its date
136	  and session id).
137	- `Reason` — why the element says what it says.
138	- `Actor` — who decided: the person by GitHub handle with their role (`@handle (owner)`,
139	  `(maintainer)`, `(contributor)`), or the run (`the growth-promote run, merged by @handle (owner)`).
140	  Never an email.
141	- `Model` — the model that wrote the decision, as the harness tells the appending session or as
142	  the landing commit's trailer names it.
143	- `Mechanism` — the carrier and its trigger, and why: the ladder rung it landed on and why the
144	  rungs above could not carry it; for a check, its scope, its gate and its severity; for a skill,
145	  its load triggers and the paths or calls they name; for a task, its precondition and policy.
146	  This is the field the log exists for most, and a `born`, `converted`, `moved`,
147	  `trigger-changed`, `policy-changed` or `severity-changed` entry always carries it.
148	- `Rejected` — the alternatives, each with its drawback.
149	- `Retire when` — the test a future review reaffirms the element against.
150	- `Landed` — the pull request or commit that landed the decision, and the pack version that
151	  shipped it (`#1151 · pack version 60821.1`), so a reader can go from the decision to the diff and
152	  to the members that received it. It is a locator, not a proof: the proof, where one exists, is
153	  in `Source` (the failing run, the measurement, the document).
154	
155	### What is a decision
156	
157	An entry is owed for any change to a carrier's normalized text, to a skill's trigger or
158	description, to a task's policy, to a check's severity, scope or gate; for a conversion, a split,
159	a merge, a move or a retirement; and for a reaffirmation that produced **new** evidence or changed
160	`Retire when`. No entry is owed for whitespace, a code comment in a coded check, a fixture, a
161	test, a README row, a version bump, or a reaffirmation that found the recorded reason still holds
162	— that run's pull request body is its record, and a row that says "still true" every week is the
163	data explosion this design refuses.
164	
165	A sweep that rewords many elements under one guideline change writes one entry per affected
166	element, one line each, citing the decision once where it was made — which is itself an element
167	change: the rule that states the guideline (in `basics` or `claudinite-growth`) carries the full
168	entry, and every moved or reworded element cites it.
169	
170	### `declined.md`
171	
172	Beside the element files, a pack keeps one unbound log of the candidates it turned down: each
173	entry `## <date> · declined · <the candidate in a few words>` with `Source`, `Reason` and
174	`Actor`. An extraction pass that drops a candidate worth remembering, and a conversion pass whose
175	verdict is "not checkable" or whose owner said no, write here; the next pass reads it before
176	nominating. A technical verdict is re-derivable later and says so with its date; an owner's
177	rejection is settled.
178	
179	## 2. Where it lives, and what never touches it
180	
181	- **Location.** `packs/<pack>/provenance/` in a canon; `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/provenance/`
182	  in a member. The tree declares it, as it declares the rest of a pack.
183	- **Never vendored.** The vendor set drops a pack-root `provenance/` the way it drops `test/`,
184	  `docs/` and `updates/`, pinned by a test over the real corpus so the exclusion cannot go vacuous.
185	  A member mounting a canon pack receives the guidelines, not the reasoning, and never another
186	  organisation's decision log.
187	- **Never loaded.** No `@` import, no skill mount, no session-summary token count. The marker at
188	  the end of a rule is the whole of what reaches a session, and it invites the reader nowhere: no
189	  rule names the folder, links it, or asks anyone to follow anything.
190	- **Never barrier-scanned.** A provenance file references what it explains — other packs, `docs/`,
191	  member repositories, retired mechanisms — so the barrier config carves `provenance/` out of every
192	  guarded region. Where the carve-out grammar cannot spell a folder one level below a `siblings`
193	  root, the grammar gains that form; never a bespoke exclusion in the scanner.
194	- **Opaque to every pack-walking check that judges carriers** — the rule-index drift guard, the
195	  prose size band, the doc-pointer resolver, the enforcement-narration check: a file under
196	  `provenance/` is neither prose nor code to them.
197	
198	## 3. Who writes, and with what
199	
200	Every flow that creates or changes an element appends, in the same change:
201	
202	| Flow | Appends |
203	|---|---|
204	| `growth-extract` (activity and conversations) | `born` per landed lesson, and the marker on the rule; a conversation-born lesson's `Source` names the capture's date and session id; `declined.md` for a candidate dropped for a reason worth keeping |
205	| `prose-to-checks` and `canon-prose-to-checks` | `converted` on the element, carrying the deletion-test verdict (prose deleted, or kept and why); `declined.md` for a rule judged not checkable, dated |
206	| `growth-dedup` | `retired` (superseded by the canon element it names), `weakened` (a strip), `reworded` |
207	| `rule-revalidation`, `canon-rule-revalidation`, `revalidate-from-source` | `reaffirmed` only with new evidence or a changed `Retire when`; `reworded` or `retired` for a correction |
208	| `growth-promote` | on the canon side the local file, reduced (§4), a `promoted` entry, and the marker on the promoted rule; the local file stays until dedup retires it |
209	| `generate-project-instructions`, `learning-a-technology` | `pack` and one `born` per element, citing the evidence set or the dated sources |
210	| an attended session editing a carrier or a README | `changing-pack-elements`, the skill forced on every pack file (below), which ends with the append |
211	
212	The mechanics are one helper, `provenance.mjs` in `claudinite-growth`, vendored so a member runs it
213	from the mount and the canon from the repo root:
214	
215	| Command | Does |
216	|---|---|
217	| `mark <pack>` | creates an empty file for every check, skill, task and the manifest that none names, and for every unmarked rule appends a proposed marker to the rule and creates the file it names — the slugs are proposals a maintainer refines before the change lands |
218	| `append <pack> <element> --kind <kind> [--changed]` | validates and appends the entry read from stdin; `--changed` appends the same entry to every element the working tree's diff touched |
219	| `check <pack>` | the parser the check uses, run by hand; prints what each file is named by |
220	| `convert-references <pack>` | the migration of a `references.md` (§6) |
221	| `reduce <file>` | the promotion reduction (§4) |
222	| `history <pack> <element>` | the backfill brief: the carrier's commits through every rename, a pickaxe on the rule's text, the pull requests those commits name, the `VERSIONS.md` rows naming them, the README's history sentences, the tracker comments |
223	
224	`append` refuses an entry that matches the capture scrub's secret patterns: a decision log is prose
225	an agent writes, and the one place a token could land is the one place nothing else scans.
226	
227	### The forced skill
228	
229	One skill in `claudinite-growth`, `changing-pack-elements`, is forced by
230	`force-load-on-file-edits-paths` on every file of a pack that a decision can change, in a local
231	pack and on a canon's shelf alike, through the two-root patterns the pack's `writing-pack-prose`
232	already uses (`**/packs/*/…` matches `.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/` in a member and
233	`packs/<pack>/` in a canon):
234	
235	| Forced on | Because |
236	|---|---|
237	| `RULES.md`, `skills/**` | a rule's wording and modality, a skill's body, description and triggers |
238	| `worldRules/**`, `workRules/**`, `declared-checks.json` | a check's gate, scope, severity and text |
239	| `tasks/**` | a task's preconditions, policy and worker |
240	| `pack.mjs` | the fingerprint, requirements, routing and seeding |
241	| `README.md` | the one file with no skill today, and the one that history creeps back into |
242	| `provenance/**` | a hand edit of a file that is otherwise appended by the helper |
243	
244	The skill is short and states three things: which kind of entry this edit owes and the `append`
245	command that writes it; what the README carries and what it does not (the paragraph above, in
246	the imperative); and that a file under `.claudinite/shared/` is never edited, which the lifecycle
247	pack's rule already says. It names no corpus, as a growth skill must, so the same skill serves the
248	shelf; `claudinite-canon-curation` adds no twin, only the rules below. The skills that already
249	load on these edits keep their subjects — `writing-pack-prose` the prose, `writing-tasks` the task
250	contract, `writing-repo-scanning-checks` the check — and none of them learns the append:
251	`writing-repo-scanning-checks` is the basics pack's, and a growth mechanism written into another
252	pack's skill is the pack-to-pack dependency the curation rules refuse. The cost is a second skill
253	loaded on a prose, task or check edit, and the first skill ever loaded on a README edit.
254	
255	### The rules that say so
256	
257	The skill fires at the edit; three rules say the same thing where a session reads rules, so a
258	session that plans a pack change knows the shape before the hook holds its first edit:
259	
260	| Pack | Rule |
261	|---|---|
262	| `claudinite-canon-curation` | **Writing a pack's `README.md`** — how a repo uses the pack and its elements: when it activates, what each check demands, when a skill is reached for, what the task does. Never how an element came to be, what it replaced or how it is maintained: a date, a pull request number, an "until" or a "kept as it was" is an entry on the element's provenance file, and the maintainer's method is the growth skills'. |
263	| `claudinite-canon-curation` | **Changing a carrier on the shelf** — a rule, a skill's trigger, a check's gate or severity, a task's policy — lands with the entry on its provenance file in the same change; the forced skill names the kind. The existing rule on descriptive prose in `RULES.md` gains the same destination: description to the module header and the README, rationale and history to the element's file. |
264	| `claudinite-growth` | **Recording a local pack change** keeps its verdict — no changelog file, the commit and its pull request are the record of *what* changed — and gains its complement: the *decision* is the entry on the element's provenance file, which the change carries. |
265	
266	The home's own local pack carries one rule that names the old destination — a design doc whose
267	system is built moves "an owner-decision record with its rationale" into a module header or a
268	pack README — and that destination becomes the element's provenance file; the section-by-section
269	verification it asks for is unchanged.
270	
271	## 4. Promotion, and the reduction that makes a shared canon safe
272	
273	A lesson promoted from a member's local pack travels with its provenance: promote copies the
274	element's file into the canon pack's `provenance/`, ends the promoted rule with the marker, and
275	appends `promoted · from a member's local pack (<canon PR>)`. The canon's version of the file is
276	therefore the full history of the guideline, not a history that starts at promotion. A slug that
277	collides on the canon side is suffixed there, and the promoted rule's marker takes the suffixed
278	name; the local file is never renamed.
279	
280	What must not leave the repo is rewritten before the copy lands, and the rule is one read of the
281	canon repository's visibility at promote time, never a setting:
282	
283	| In the local pack (stays as written) | In a private canon | In a public canon |
284	|---|---|---|
285	| `Actor` — `@handle (role)` | kept | the role only |
286	| a session id or link | dropped | dropped |
287	| a quoted phrase (at most one sentence, as the extraction skills already limit) | dropped; the paraphrase stays | dropped |
288	| `owner/repo#n` references and `Landed` locators | kept | `a member repository` |
289	| product, file and path names in `Source` | generalized, as the promoted rule itself is | generalized |
290	| `Model`, dates, kinds, `Reason`, `Mechanism`, `Rejected`, `Retire when` | kept | kept |
291	
292	The policy is structural — what crosses a repository boundary is reduced by what that boundary is —
293	so no member configures an identity policy and no canon has one to get wrong. A promote pull
294	request is owner-gated (`automerge: nothing`) exactly as today, so a reviewer's eyes are the last
295	guard on what the reduction is not built to see: a product name inside a `Reason`.
296	
297	## 5. Pack kinds
298	
299	| Kind | Provenance | Crosses a boundary |
300	|---|---|---|
301	| repo-local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) | required; the origin of most decisions; actors by handle | only through promote, reduced |
302	| canon pack (`packs/`), hidden packs included | required; actors by handle in a private canon, by role once public | vendored never; forked by clone with the folder intact |
303	| the home's structural local pack | as a repo-local pack | never |
304	| organisation pack (a second canon in the organisation's registry) | as a canon pack; the organisation's release task is a promote target and source like any other | as a canon pack |
305	| vendor-authored pack | as a canon pack in the vendor's repository; a consumer never receives it; a consumer's decision *about* it — an `accept` waiver with its `reason`, an override naming the element's id — lives where it is declared and needs no file | never |
306	| process and rules-of-thumb packs (`basics`, testing, git) | as a canon pack; `Source` cites the practice, book or incident; `Retire when` may be a judgment ("the practice is abandoned corpus-wide") and says so | as a canon pack |
307	| a pack minted from project evidence | `pack`'s `born` cites the evidence set or the dated sources | as a canon pack |
308	| a stub pack with no rules | `pack` only | as a canon pack |
309	| personal preferences — a pack of one reader, whose rules file is the person's `<email>.md` in the store | each preference is an element with a marker; its files sit **beside** the store, at `<path>-provenance/<email>/`, because the store's own check keeps `<path>/` flat and addresses nothing but `<email>.md` there; written by the session that edits the preference; the person is the actor; coverage advisory, as everything in that pack is | never — a preference is never promoted, by the extraction rules that already bar it |
310	
311	A consumer that forks an element from a canon into its local pack (an override) writes a `born`
312	entry citing the canon element by its id; the canon's file is not copied down.
313	
314	Preferences pay the marker like any rules file — a few tokens per preference in the injected
315	text — and their entries are the shortest the log holds: the person is the actor, the request is
316	the reason, and what the file answers months later is when a preference was set or changed and
317	what prompted it.
318	
319	## 6. Backfill, conversion, and the standing mechanism
320	
321	Two things bring existing packs onto the convention, and both are mechanisms rather than passes
322	someone remembers to run.
323	
324	**Marking is one mechanical pass.** `mark` over every pack creates an empty file per unnamed
325	carrier and ends every unmarked rule with a proposed marker. It therefore edits every `RULES.md`
326	and every `SKILL.md` that carries unmarked rules — prose that vendors — so the `pack-version-bump`
327	task cuts every touched pack's version once the pass lands, and the nightly converge delivers a
328	prose-only change the way it delivers any other. From that commit every carrier names a file, the
329	integrity check (§7) holds, and the only thing missing is history.
330	
331	**Filling is a task, one pack per run, until no empty file remains.** The backfill task —
332	`provenance-backfill` in `claudinite-growth` over a member's local packs, its twin in
333	`claudinite-canon-curation` over the shelf — has the precondition "an empty provenance file exists
334	under the corpus", runs weekly and is woken by hand for the first pass. Each run takes one pack:
335	`history` gathers the evidence per element, the agent derives the `born` entry and the
336	decision-bearing entries from that source **before** re-reading the rule, then diffs against what
337	the rule implied. A field the evidence does not carry is left out; a fabricated rationale would
338	let a future review reaffirm a rule on false grounds, which is worse than no rationale at all.
339	An element whose history the evidence does not reach at all gets a `born` entry that says only
340	what is known — the date and commit it first appears in — and stays as short as that. The same
341	run trims the pack's README: each sentence of history it holds — the "distilled from" paragraph,
342	the "until #n", the "kept as it was", the mechanism's reasons — is evidence the run has already
343	read, so it moves onto the entry it evidences and leaves the README, which keeps only what §1
344	says a README carries. The task's pull request is one pack's backfill and one README's trim,
345	reviewed as such; the README is the one vendored file the run touches, so the pack's version is
346	cut once by automation as for any prose change.
347	
348	**`references.md` converts mechanically.** `convert-references` turns each entry into an entry of
349	the element it keys — `RULES-n` resolves through the rule carrying the marker `(n)`, `<skill>-n`
350	to that skill, `check:<id>` to that check — as a `born` entry dated by the entry's own adding
351	commit, its reaffirmation sentence as `Retire when`, the rest as `Reason` and `Landed`; then
352	rewrites each numeric marker to the slug its element takes and deletes the file. A skill bullet
353	that carries a numeric marker today has a recorded history, so it becomes an element of its own
354	with a slug marker and a file — about fifty bullets across twenty skills. A pack-root
355	`references.md` that still exists is a finding: advisory through the conversion window the
356	migration states, blocking after it, with the command in the fix text. In a member, the backfill
357	task runs the conversion as its first step.
358	
359	**No README is trimmed by the marking pass.** Which sentence of a README is history is a
360	judgment made with the element's evidence in hand, so it belongs to the backfill run and not to
361	the mechanical pass; until a pack's run has come, its README reads as today, and nothing loads it.
362	
363	## 7. The check: `provenance-integrity`
364	
365	A coded rule in `claudinite-growth` (a declared check cannot read a bullet whose last line and
366	bold trigger wrap), over both roots, replacing `references-integrity`.
367	
368	World scope, blocking:
369	
370	1. every check, skill and task id, and the manifest, names a live file; every `RULES.md` bullet
371	   ends with a marker, and every marker — in a `RULES.md`, where it is required, or in a
372	   `SKILL.md`, where it is optional — names a live file; a rule with no marker, a marker naming
373	   no live file, and a live file no carrier names are each a finding naming the carrier or the
374	   file. A live file is one whose last entry is not `retired`;
375	2. every file parses: the entry grammar, a kind in the vocabulary, dates in order, a field
376	   vocabulary the entry keeps to;
377	3. a file with entries opens with `born`, and the mechanism-bearing kinds carry `Mechanism`; an
378	   empty file is reported as pending history, at advisory, since it is the backfill task's
379	   worklist and not a defect;
380	4. a pack-root `references.md` is the migration finding above.
381	
382	Work scope, blocking:
383	
384	5. a carrier whose normalized text changed in this change names a file that gained an entry in
385	   this change — comments stripped, whitespace collapsed, the marking pass exempt by its `since`;
386	6. a provenance file changed in this change lost no line, and its new lines follow the last
387	   existing entry;
388	7. a carrier deleted in this change named a file that gained a `retired` entry as its last in the
389	   same change — a removed-lines check cannot see a deleted file, so the deletion is asserted from
390	   the tree's side.
391	
392	The work-scope half is what makes the convention hold for a hand edit: the skill says append, and
393	the Stop hook says so again when the session did not.
394	
395	The preferences store is not under either root, so the preferences pack carries its own advisory
396	check, relevance-first like its siblings (inert unless this repo *is* the store): every preference
397	bullet ends with a marker naming a file under `<path>-provenance/<email>/`. It asserts existence
398	only — self-describing data, so nothing is shared between the two packs — and the grammar is
399	judged by the helper's `check`, run by the session that edits the preference.
400	
401	## 8. Invariants
402	
403	1. Every live carrier names exactly one live provenance file, and every live file is named by at
404	   least one live carrier.
405	2. A provenance file only grows. Nothing in it is ever edited or removed.
406	3. No entry describes the current rule. The carrier is the description; the entry is the
407	   decision, and its `Mechanism` is why the carrier is the carrier.
408	4. Nothing under `provenance/` reaches a session, a member's mount, a barrier scan, or a check that
409	   judges carriers; the marker is the one token a session sees.
410	5. What crosses a repository boundary is reduced (§4); what stays is written as the repository's
411	   own norms allow.
412	6. A field is written only when there is something behind it. Nothing is invented, nothing is
413	   padded, and nothing is deleted to look complete.
414	7. A reaffirmation with nothing new writes nothing.
415	8. An element's id never changes.
416	
417	## 9. Sizing, and the failure modes stated
418	
419	**Size.** The canon shelf holds roughly 560 rules, 150 checks, 60 skills, 40 tasks and 38 packs:
420	about 850 files, most under 2 KB, one to four entries each across a year of decisions; the home's
421	own local pack adds about 185. Per element the growth flows append perhaps twice a year; the
422	folder grows with decisions, not with runs, because §1 refuses the "still true" row. A pack
423	deletion removes its folder; git keeps the history, as it keeps everything else.
424	
425	- **Two runs append to one element the same night.** Both change the same end of the same file
426	  and git reports a conflict; the resolution keeps both entries in date order. It is rare by
427	  construction — two runs deciding about one element at once is a conflict on the element itself —
428	  and it is the whole answer to the merge hazard that ruled out an aggregate changelog: per-element
429	  files collide only on the element, never on the line every run would append to.
430	- **A sweep rewords forty rules.** Forty one-line entries are owed and `append --changed` writes
431	  them; the markers stay where they were, so nothing rebinds. A sweep that drops a marker while
432	  rewording leaves the rule unmarked, which the check reports.
433	- **A marker is misspelled or names a retired file.** A finding naming the rule; the fix is the
434	  file the rule meant.
435	- **Two rules carry one marker.** Legal only as a cluster the file's entries account for; a
436	  second rule that merely reused a slug takes its own.
437	- **A promoted slug collides.** Suffixed on the canon side, marker included; the local file is
438	  never renamed.
439	- **A whole element is deleted.** The file stays, its last entry `retired`: the decision to remove
440	  is a decision. A retired file is named by nothing and costs nothing.
441	- **Private text reaches the canon.** The reduction removes what it is built to see; the
442	  owner-gated promote pull request is the guard for what it is not; the scrub refuses a secret at
443	  append time.
444	- **A backfill fabricates.** A field is written only from evidence, every entry carries its
445	  `Landed` locator so a reviewer can go to the diff, and one pack per pull request keeps the
446	  review readable.
447	- **A session edits a carrier without appending.** The work-scope check fails the change at the
448	  Stop hook with the `append` command in the fix.
449	- **History creeps back into a README.** The forced skill states the scope at the edit, the
450	  curation rule states it where rules are read, and the next backfill or revalidation run over
451	  the pack reads the README as evidence and moves what it finds. No check greps a README for a
452	  date: the phrase list would be the whole check, and the skill at the edit is the cheaper guard.
453	- **A vendored copy leaks the folder.** The vendor-set test asserts over the real corpus that no
454	  `provenance/` path vendors, in the same test that pins `test/` and `docs/`.
455	
456	## 10. Decisions and their alternatives
457	
458	- **One file per element, in a folder** — over one `provenance.md` per pack. A single file is the
459	  aggregate changelog the growth pack already refuses: every run appends to the same file, two
460	  runs a night collide on it, and one element's history is interleaved with every other's. A folder
461	  of files makes each element's history its own file, its own `git log`, and its own copy on
462	  promotion. The cost is the file count, paid by no session and no member.
463	- **A slug marker naming the file** — over the numeric marker `references.md` uses, and over
464	  binding a rule by its trigger phrase with nothing in the prose. A number is stable but opaque: a
465	  reader cannot go from `(12)` to a file, and `RULES-12` says nothing about the guideline. Trigger
466	  binding costs the prose nothing but gives a rule no id — a rewording changes its identity, every
467	  sweep rebinds every header, and nothing a member writes survives the rewording of the rule it
468	  overrides. The slug is the reference and the id in one string, at a few tokens per rule, and the
469	  same string names the file, the override and the entry.
470	- **No header** — over a front matter carrying status or coverage. Coverage is derived from what
471	  names the file, and status from the last entry's kind; a header would be a second copy of each,
472	  and the one part of the file that invites editing.
473	- **A Markdown log with a line grammar** — over JSON or JSONL. A JSON array cannot be appended to;
474	  JSONL can, but a reviewer reads a decision log in a pull request and a maintainer reads it
475	  cold, and neither reads JSONL. The grammar is small enough to parse without a library.
476	- **Written at decision time** — over a log derived from git after the fact, as `VERSIONS.md` is.
477	  Git carries what changed; it never carries why, which alternative lost, or what would retire the
478	  result. Those exist only in the head of whoever decides, at the moment they decide.
479	- **Never vendored** — over shipping provenance to members so a session could read a rule's
480	  reason. A session that needs the reason to apply a rule has a rule that lacks its consequence
481	  clause, which is the prose's defect to fix; and a member's mount would carry every organisation's
482	  decision log, which is the privacy failure §4 exists to prevent.
483	- **A skill is one element** — over binding every skill bullet. A long skill is procedure, and
484	  procedure changes as a whole; thirty files for one skill is noise, and a bullet with its own
485	  history takes its own marker only when it has one.
486	- **`declined.md` per pack** — over a tracker issue's comment feed. A comment feed is one
487	  scrollable history for every candidate in the corpus; a per-pack file is read by the pass that
488	  is about to re-nominate in that pack, which is the read that prevents the rework.
489	- **One forced skill for the append and the README scope** — over teaching every editing skill
490	  the append. Three skills from two packs load on carrier edits today, one of them the basics
491	  pack's, and a growth mechanism cannot be written into it; one growth skill states the append
492	  once, reaches the README that no skill reaches today, and serves the shelf without a curation
493	  twin. The cost is one more skill loaded per pack edit.
494	- **The README trimmed by the backfill run** — over a separate sweep, and over leaving READMEs as
495	  they are. The run holds the evidence each history sentence points at, so moving the sentence is
496	  the same read; a sweep would re-derive the element for every sentence, and a README that keeps
497	  its history keeps a second, unmaintained copy of the log beside the log.
498	- **Handles reduced by the canon's visibility** — over one identity policy everywhere. A local pack
499	  and a private canon sit beside git logs that already name their authors; a public canon is read
500	  by people who never saw that repo. The boundary is the policy, and it is read, not set.
501	
502	## 11. What the log buys beyond the record
503	
504	- **Overrides and waivers can name a rule** and survive its rewording: the marker is the stable id
505	  the layering design requires, and it exists for every rule from the marking pass on.
506	- **Mechanism choices become reviewable**: why a skill loads on these paths and not those, why a
507	  check is advisory, why a task's precondition reads as it does — each with the alternative it
508	  beat, so the next person to touch the trigger knows what it was for.
509	- **Revalidation reads `Retire when` per element, with the history behind it**, rather than one
510	  sentence that was overwritten at the last correction.
511	- **Conversion passes stop re-deriving**: `declined.md` and `converted` entries are the memory the
512	  prose-to-checks skill already asks for.
513	- **Promotion carries strength**: a canon reviewer reads that a lesson was born in one member,
514	  reaffirmed in another, and converted to a check in a third.
515	- **Conflicts between rules become resolvable**: both sides' reasons and evidence are in front of
516	  whoever judges them, and a rule born from an incident is weighed differently from one born from
517	  vendor documentation.
518	- **A false premise is findable**: when a platform changes, grepping `provenance/` for the source
519	  (a documentation URL, a Chrome version, an API name) lists every element that rests on it.
520	- **Demotion has a denominator**: a check's blocking-firing rate is read against the reason it was
521	  written, not against a guess.
522	- **Attribution becomes data**: which decisions were a person's and which a model's, and which
523	  model — read as a window against the previous window, never as a total — so a retirement rate
524	  per authoring model is a number something measures.
525	- **The conversion inventory's class column becomes derivable** from `converted` and `declined`
526	  entries instead of hand-dated corrections.
527	- **A README shrinks to its reader**: a person adopting a pack reads how to use it, and the
528	  history that read as description — a third of some READMEs today — is on the file that can
529	  answer for it.
530	- **An audit can answer what shaped the rules**: incidents, documents and requests, and never a
531	  member's product source.
532	
533	## 12. Retrospective brief
534	
535	Filed at the merge that completes the mechanism, horizon one week after the marking pass lands
536	on `main`; a second reading a week after the backfill task's precondition first reads false.
537	
538	- **Expected amounts.** One marking commit creating an empty file per unnamed carrier and a marker
539	  per unmarked rule (about 850 files on the shelf, 185 in the home's local pack; the count is
540	  `mark`'s own report and the file count under `provenance/`). Backfill: one pull request per
541	  run, one pack each, so about 36 canon runs and one local; forced daily the shelf completes inside
542	  two weeks, weekly inside a season. Growth flows: a handful of `born` entries a week fleet-wide,
543	  read from the extract pull requests' diffs; zero `reaffirmed` entries from a revalidation run
544	  that found everything still true. `references.md` files on the shelf: 21 before the conversion,
545	  0 after; in members' local packs the same fall on each member's first backfill run. About
546	  fifty skill bullets with numeric markers today become elements of their own. The session-start
547	  summary's prose token weight rises by the marker count and no more. README bytes on the shelf:
548	  about 230 KB across 37 files before the backfill; each run's pull request reports the pack's
549	  before and after, and the shelf total falls as the runs come.
550	- **Expected behaviours.** Every promote pull request carries a reduced provenance file and a
551	  marker per promoted lesson (read from the promote PR's diff). A hand edit of a carrier in an
552	  attended session appends in the same commit (read from the `provenance-integrity` firing counts
553	  in the usage fold: a firing that the session then fixed is the check working; a firing rate near
554	  zero with carrier edits flowing means sessions append unprompted). Every `trigger-changed` and
555	  `policy-changed` entry carries a `Mechanism` that names the alternative it beat.
556	- **Misuse.** An entry that restates the rule; an edited or removed line, which the check reports;
557	  a README edit made without the forced skill (the hook's `skill-not-loaded` count for
558	  `changing-pack-elements`); a history sentence written into a README after its trim;
559	  an `Actor` that is an email; a session id or a quote in a canon file; a provenance path in a
560	  member's mount; a rule whose marker names a file and whose file says nothing about that rule; a
561	  placeholder value where a field should have been omitted.
562	- **Overuse.** `reaffirmed` entries with no new evidence; sweep entries longer than a line; a
563	  `declined.md` that grows by more than a few entries a week in one pack; backfill runs that
564	  produce one-line `born` entries for a pack whose history is plainly in git.
565	- **Underuse.** Elements still empty a season after marking; extract runs whose diff adds a rule
566	  and no entry (only possible outside a Stop hook — a direct API write — and the check on the
567	  branch would say so); promote pull requests with no provenance file beside a promoted rule;
568	  overrides and waivers still naming rules by quoting their text after the marker exists; a
569	  `trigger-changed` entry with no `Mechanism`; READMEs of backfilled packs still carrying an
570	  "until #n".
571	- **Per decision, what would show the alternative was right.** The slug marker: the prose token
572	  weight rising by more than the marker count predicts, or markers dropped in reword sweeps more
573	  than once each — the marker was noisier than rationed, and a number or nothing was cheaper. One
574	  file per element: conflict resolutions on `provenance/` files more than once a month — the
575	  collision was not rare. Skill as one element: entries on a skill file that name bullets more
576	  often than the skill, month after month. No header: a check or a reader that needed coverage
577	  written down after all. Handles by visibility: a review that could not judge a decision without
578	  knowing who took it, or a name in a public canon that should not have been there. One forced
579	  skill: sessions that loaded it on a README edit and changed nothing the skill speaks to (a
580	  typo, a link), often enough that the load is the cost and the README should leave the list.
581	- **Cheap to re-examine:** the backfill cadence and its one-pack-per-run size, the conversion
582	  window's date, the advisory grade on empty files, the entry-field vocabulary, the slug length,
583	  the forced skill's path list.
584	  **Expensive:** the file grammar, the id rule (a marker is the id and never changes), the
585	  never-vendored and never-loaded properties, the reduction's boundary rule.
586	- **Metrics the review needs, and the read.** File and entry counts: `git ls-files
587	  'packs/*/provenance/*.md'` and a grep for `^## ` on the shelf. Marker counts: a grep for the
588	  marker pattern over `packs/*/RULES.md`. Firing counts for `provenance-integrity`: the usage
589	  fold's per-check series. Promote coverage: the diffs of the pull requests the `Claudinite
590	  tracker: Promote to Canon` issue's comments name. Backfill progress: the task's run records and
591	  the empty-file count `mark` reports. Conflict resolutions: commits touching `provenance/` whose
592	  parents both touched the same file.
